newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL DROP JUNINHO FOR FRANCE TOURNAMENT, COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL DROP JUNINHO FOR FRANCE TOURNAMENT, COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo has left midfielder Juninho out of his squad for June's four-team tournament in France and Copa America in Bolivia.

Juninho, whose English side Middlesbrough have lost the battle against relegation from the premier league, was not among the foreign-based players named by Zagallo on Wednesday for the two competitions and a friendly away to Norway on May 31.

His omission means that, for the time being at least, Juninho appears to have lost his battle with Palmeiras midfielder Djalminha, whom Zagallo confirmed would be included when the home-based players are officially picked next week.

The two players are seen in Brazil as direct rivals for one of the two attacking midfield places, with Leonardo of French club Paris St Germain and Giovanni of Spain's Barcelona fighting for the other. Both Leonardo and Giovanni were included on Tuesday.

"This doesn't mean that he is not an excellent player," Zagallo said of Juninho. "He is not out of contention for future selections. This is my option for these competitions. Time will provide the final answer for the World Cup."
Juninho has been a regular fixture in both the full and Olympic teams since 1995.
Juninho has hinted strongly that Saturday's English F.A. Cup final against Chelsea at Wembley will be his last game for Middlesbrough.

"I have to think of my career and see what is best for me," he said on Wednesday. "What's most important for me is to be in the Brazil squad. And to be in the Brazil squad you have to play in good teams."
"Nobody likes playing in the first division."

Zagallo, who is building a side to defend the World Cup in France next year, said he wanted to see how the extremely gifted but volatile Djalminha fared against European opposition. Djalminha has played only four low-key friendlies against modest opposition.
Djalminha, sacked by Flamengo earlier in his career after clashing with a team mate on the field, was sent off for the third time this year while playing for his club on Tuesday.
"Most of the players have been sent off playing for their clubs," said Zagallo. "If I avoided picking players who have received red cards I would not be able to form a team."
"If a player commits an act of indiscipline in the national team, then he will be punished."

There were no other surprises with Barcelona striker Ronaldo duly included and 1994 World Cup captain Dunga, recalled after nearly two years' absence for last month's game with Mexico, keeping his place.
Zagallo promised that Brazil would play with flair in the upcoming games which represent their stiffest test since the 1995 Copa America when they lost on penalties in the final to hosts Uruguay.

"We want to return to 1958 and 1970 in which artistry was always important," he said. "I want other coaches around to think the same way, not to send their teams on to the field to stop the opposition from playing."

Foreign-based players in the squad: Aldair (Roma), Cesar Sampaio (Yokohama Flugels), Dunga (Jubilo Iwata), Flavio Conceicao (Deportivo Coruna), Giovanni (Barcelona), Leonardo (Paris St Germain), Mauro Silva (Deportivo Coruna), Roberto Carlos (Real Madrid), Ronaldo (Barcelona), Ze Roberto (Real Madrid), Ze Maria (Parma).
